result.title: ViTrust: Learning 3D Observation Trust for Deformable Physical World Models
result.summary: Learning deformable physical world models requires dynamics that generalize beyond observed motion. Accurate reconstruction alone does not ensure accurate future prediction, motivating us to learn how observations should influence physical identification. However, visual reliability alone does not determine how informative an observation is about physical dynamics. We propose ViTrust to learn 3D observation trust, determining how strongly each tracked point influences physical identification. Its key design is a visual-contact trust adapter that combines pointwise spatiotemporal evidence with interaction history on a persistent contact graph to predict time-varying observation weights. A single-stage, shared-forward objective jointly optimizes these weights and physical parameters through weighted geometry and correspondence losses, with constraints to prevent observation-weight collapse. All learning uses only the observed prefix. The fitted physics remains fixed for future prediction under supplied controls. Experiments on real-world sequences demonstrate improved future prediction over the evaluated baselines, alongside qualitative demonstrations of novel-control rollouts and cross-object transfer.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ViTrust，用视觉—接触信任适配器在持久接触图上结合逐点时空证据与交互历史，预测随时间变化的观测权重，并以单阶段共享前向目标联合优化权重与物理参数，同时加约束避免权重坍缩，全部学习仅用观测前缀。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「学习每个观测对内部状态识别的影响强度」及防权重坍缩、接触图上的历史记忆设计，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与加权、证据贡献分配机制的借鉴，属跨域迁移推测。
